framework_note: CACI is a defense-IT services prime, not a weapons-system OEM. The FY2024 10-K names NO specific PE numbers and NO J-Book-named programs. Customer concentration is disclosed at the agency level (DoD = 74.4% of FY24 revenue), not at the program-element level. As a result the J-Book divergence pattern has very little leverage on this filing: pentagon_jbook is structurally NOT_FOUND for the company because (a) the J-Book corpus does not list CACI as a primary contractor on any of its 410 PEs (CACI is typically a 3-letter-agency / mission-services prime whose work appears under OMA/RDTE pots rather than weapons PEs), and (b) the filing itself does not name PEs to look up. The strongest verifier here is usaspending: CACI shows 3,568 contracts and $21.7B lifetime federal obligations (RECURRING_FEDERAL), validating customer-concentration claims. This is the kind of company where the J-Book framework produces mostly UNVERIFIABLE — which is the correct answer, not a failure mode.

The J-Book divergence pattern (the cohort thesis) does not apply structurally to CACI's revenue model. Per heuristic 7, NOT_FOUND treated as PASS-equivalent given strong usaspending corroboration.

Primary EW program is FUNDED_STEADY — these are areas Pentagon is actively budgeting in.

C-UAS coverage gap in the corpus (UNVERIFIABLE for that sub-claim) but the closest J-Book signal (EW) is steady-funded. CACI's capability narrative aligns with what the Pentagon is paying for.

summary.headline: No J-Book divergence detected. CACI's FY2024 10-K names no specific PE numbers; revenue concentration is at agency (DoD = 74.4%) not program-element level; USAspending corroborates the federal-revenue concentration ($21.7B lifetime, 3,568 contracts, 12+ agencies); pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for the contractor is structurally expected for a services prime and not adverse. acq_coherence returns COHERENT_ROLLUP. Filing passes the J-Book divergence test by construction (low surface area for the test) and passes the orthogonal usaspending cross-check.
